coo_office.primary_setup: Your COO needs a one-page memo by tomorrow on how your team will use AI in quarterly planning. You are about to ask ChatGPT to write the first draft from last quarter's slides and a Slack export.
coo_office.primary_stakes: The whole leadership team will read it. Wrong names, made-up numbers, or skipping Legal and Finance will be embarrassing and hard to walk back.
coo_office.complication_inject: While polishing the draft, someone on your team pasted real customer names and next year's targets into a shared ChatGPT thread.
coo_office.standards_prompt: If everyone in your function starts using ChatGPT on memos and plans that others act on, what would you want them to check before they hit send?

product.primary_setup: Your product manager wants ChatGPT to write the spec for a new checkout change by Friday. The feature handles card payments and needs Compliance sign-off.
product.primary_stakes: If the requirements are wrong, or the draft invents a rule that does not exist, you slip the launch or ship something Compliance has not approved.
product.complication_inject: Someone pasted real customer account numbers into a shared ChatGPT chat while working on the spec.
product.standards_prompt: When your team uses ChatGPT on specs that engineers will build, what quality bar would you set before anyone commits to the work?

ops.primary_setup: ChatGPT drafted a refund apology for an upset VIP customer. Your frontline agent wants to send it in one click from the helpdesk.
ops.primary_stakes: The tone, the facts, and what you are offering have to match policy. A wrong reply goes straight to the customer and is hard to undo.
ops.complication_inject: The draft sounds warm, but it offers a bigger refund than policy allows and promises an exception your team cannot honor.
ops.standards_prompt: What can frontline agents send on their own, and what should they escalate before a customer sees it?

gtm.primary_setup: Marketing wants ChatGPT to write tomorrow's launch email and landing page for a new savings product.
gtm.primary_stakes: Every claim has to be true and on-brand. Generic or overstated copy hurts trust and can create compliance issues.
gtm.complication_inject: The draft includes a performance number that is roughly true internally but has never been approved for public use.
gtm.standards_prompt: How would brand, legal, and sales agree on what ChatGPT can draft versus what stays fully human-written?

people.primary_setup: Your company announces a return-to-office policy next week. Someone in People Ops used ChatGPT to draft the company-wide email and a short guide for line managers on how to explain it to their teams.
people.primary_stakes: If the email makes hybrid sound more flexible than the rule really is, employees will act on the wrong expectation and HR will field angry messages.
people.complication_inject: The ChatGPT draft reads friendly, but it says people can work from home twice a week. The approved policy is one day.
people.standards_prompt: Before any people-related email goes to staff, who has to read it, and what would you tell your team about putting employee details into ChatGPT?

people_ta.primary_setup: A recruiter on your team used ChatGPT to draft a batch of rejection emails and a first-draft offer letter for a senior hire. They want to send them by end of day.
people_ta.primary_stakes: Wrong tone, wrong role details, or a benefit that is not in the approved offer template can upset candidates and create legal exposure.
people_ta.complication_inject: The offer letter draft adds a signing bonus your comp band does not allow, but it reads confident and polished.
people_ta.standards_prompt: Before any candidate-facing email or offer leaves your team, who reviews it, and what would you tell recruiters about pasting applicant details into ChatGPT?

risk.primary_setup: A partner bank sends a vendor security form. Your colleague used ChatGPT to fill in the section on how you store customer data and how long you keep it.
risk.primary_stakes: If you overstate what you do, or miss how long data is retained, you create audit and legal exposure.
risk.complication_inject: The draft says you delete all prompts within 24 hours. That is not true for the tool your team actually uses.
risk.standards_prompt: How would you turn your data-retention policy into simple day-to-day rules people can follow when they answer forms like this?

fin.primary_setup: You owe a section of next week's board deck on revenue and growth. A colleague used ChatGPT to draft the charts and narrative from a spreadsheet.
fin.primary_stakes: A confident wrong number in a board pack is worse than a slide that lands a day late.
fin.complication_inject: The chart swaps Q2 and Q3 growth, but the write-up still sounds sure of itself.
fin.standards_prompt: What checks would you want before any number or forecast leaves your desk, whether or not ChatGPT helped write it?

gm.primary_setup: Leadership asks you to choose one AI project for the next six months: automating support replies, or improving sales forecasting. Both teams sent business cases — partly drafted with ChatGPT.
gm.primary_stakes: Budget, risk, and leadership attention are limited. Vendor demos often look better than real life.
gm.complication_inject: One vendor's demo used success numbers that do not match how your actual data behaves.
gm.standards_prompt: How would you pressure-test a vendor's claims and decide when to stop a pilot before you scale it?
